c722-section-1-section-1-test-q2.explanation: A portfolio is the set of projects and programs a company engages in to improve its operations. A program, by contrast, is a group of related projects that support the company's goals and objectives (Lesson 1.6).

c722-section-1-section-1-test-q7.explanation: This is a communication plan. The table's columns (audience, method of communication, who drafts and presents, due dates) are what a communication plan records, and each project needs its own stated plan (Lesson 2.3).

c722-section-1-lesson-1-quiz-q1.explanation: A project is a targeted, temporary effort with a specific start date and end date, which separates it from ongoing operations (Lessons 1.3 and 1.4).

c722-section-4-lesson-1-quiz-q6.explanation: Traditional methods follow a linear, sequential path: define, plan, execute, and close, with virtually no overlap. Plan is the second phase (Lesson 1.6).

c722-section-5-lesson-1-quiz-q2.explanation: Scope verification is the fourth step of the scope management process, and it falls in the closing phase of the project life cycle.
